title: Connection to Country and Place
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:18Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank point, geo-connection-country, covers Country and connection through family and culture, but it does not teach the brief's link between connection and wellbeing or liveability, and adding that idea goes beyond the small changes allowed for an adapt.

draft.title: Connection to Country and Place
card: for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples, Country includes land, waters, sky and kin. It is a living whole that people belong to, not only a piece of land.
a location that has meaning for a person or group. People can feel a strong connection to a Place through their experiences and memories there.
Being connected to Country and Place supports identity, culture and wellbeing. It links people to their stories, their family and their responsibilities to care for Country.
Because of this, a place can be liveable partly because people feel connected to it. Being able to stay on and look after Country is part of that.
draft.remember: Country is land, waters, sky and kin. Connection to it supports identity, culture and wellbeing, and so liveability.

a.q: Which best describes Country for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples?
opts: Land, waters, sky and kin that people belong to
Only the area of land that a person owns
A town that has a council and a main street
A national park that visitors can camp in
a.why: Country includes land, waters, sky and kin, and people belong to it. It is not only land a person owns, which is the tempting but narrower idea.
a.clue: Country is bigger than land alone.

b.q: An Aboriginal community in Victoria cares for a river and passes on its stories to young people. How does this connection add to liveability?
opts: It supports identity, culture and wellbeing
It makes the river's distance from shops shorter
It guarantees the town has more public transport
It removes the need for any other services
b.why: Caring for Country and sharing its stories strengthens identity, culture and wellbeing, which helps make the place liveable. It does not change distances or replace services.
b.clue: Think about what connection gives people, not what it builds.

a.best: Land, waters, sky and kin that people belong to

b.best: It supports identity, culture and wellbeing

problems.detail: The card defines Place (capital P) as any location with meaning for a person or group. In the Victorian and Australian Curriculum, 'Country/Place' pairs Country (used mainly by Aboriginal Peoples) with Place (used by Torres Strait Islander Peoples for their lands, seas and connections). This card mixes that up with the general geography idea of place, so students learn the term wrongly.

check.summary: Both questions are sound and have one clear right answer. The card defines 'Place' as a general meaningful location rather than the Torres Strait Islander term in 'Country/Place', which misrepresents the curriculum term and should be corrected.

proposal.title: Connection to Country and Place
card: a word used mainly by Aboriginal Peoples. Country includes land, waters, sky and kin. It is a living whole that people belong to, not only a piece of land.
a word used by many Torres Strait Islander Peoples for their islands, seas, sky and kin. With a capital P, it means more than the everyday word place.
Being connected to Country and Place supports identity, culture and wellbeing. It links people to their stories, their family and their responsibilities to care for Country and Place.
Because of this, a place can be liveable partly because people feel connected to it. Being able to stay on and look after Country and Place is part of that.
proposal.remember: Connection to Country and Place supports identity, culture and wellbeing, and so helps make a place liveable.
